results.note: UncorroboratedDefinition (ingest/registry.py:37-42) is a plain optional field defaulting to None (registry.py:60) with no computed/inferred value. The test loads a registry entry that explicitly sets `uncorroborated.note` and asserts corroboration is None / uncorroborated is not None and the note text is preserved, proving the flag is only ever set by explicit YAML, never derived.

The test model_dumps both a corroborated and an uncorroborated IndicatorDefinition and asserts the resulting dicts differ and each carries the opposite field populated/None. Caveat: this proves the registry-level model is structurally distinguishable, but ingest/corroborate.py (the module that actually writes datapoints/corroborations to the DB) has no reference to `uncorroborated` at all -- grep found zero hits outside registry.py/registry.yaml/tests. So the criterion is satisfied at the level the named test operates on (registry model dump), but the claim is not wired into the real corroborations-table write path; since the AC's method is declared 'test' (not 'integration'), the named test is the contract and it passes with real assertions.

load_registry (registry.py:174-188) computes has_second_source/is_uncorroborated per raw entry and raises ValueError('... must declare exactly one corroboration declaration ...') whenever the two booleans are equal -- covering both silence (both False) and double-declaration (both True), mirroring the reject_wildcards discipline on definable_for (registry.py:62-69). The test removes the uncorroborated block from a valid entry and asserts the ValueError is raised with the matching message.

assert_registry_coverage (registry.py:191-215), the PRD-002 registry-generated coverage check, now appends a failure '{key} is missing exactly one corroboration declaration' when has_second_source == is_uncorroborated (line 201-206), extending the existing hand-kept-list-avoidance mechanism as the story's implementer notes require. The test constructs an IndicatorDefinition with neither field set and asserts AssertionError is raised matching 'corroboration declaration'.

Deterministic gate US-306-C5 (`uv run python -m ingest.registry --validate`) exited 0. Confirmed by reading the shipped ingest/registry.yaml directly: its single entry (btc_daily_close) declares `corroboration` and not `uncorroborated`, so has_second_source=True/is_uncorroborated=False are unequal and load_registry's new check does not raise.

note: All 5 criteria are backed by real, assertion-bearing named tests in tests/test_uncorroborated.py that match the story's declared AC test names exactly, plus the registry.py logic they exercise (explicit-only field, XOR validation in both load_registry and assert_registry_coverage) and a clean --validate gate. The one honest gap: the `uncorroborated` field is purely a registry/YAML-level declaration -- ingest/corroborate.py (the actual DB-writing pipeline from US-303/304/305) never references it, and the shipped registry.yaml still contains only the original btc_daily_close/corroboration entry, not a real Coin Metrics MVRV entry (the MVRV example lives only inside the test file, as a synthetic tmp_path registry). This doesn't fail any criterion since all are declared method:test and the named tests match verbatim, but the story's narrative claim -- that Coin Metrics MVRV itself now carries a registry note about upstream consolidation -- is not actually true of the shipped data, only demonstrated in a test fixture.
